facts.statement: Yacarerani is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodylomorph from the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Yacarerani (meaning "first Yacare" in Guaraní) is an extinct genus of Late Cretaceous notosuchian crocodylomorph.

facts.statement: Yacarerani was a small crocodylomorph measuring approximately 80 cm in length.
facts.quote: Yacarerani was a small crocodylomorph at around 80 cm in length.

facts.statement: Fossils of Yacarerani were found in 2002 in the Cajones Formation of Amboró National Park in central Bolivia and date to the Turonian-Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in 2002 in the Cajones Formation in Amboró National Park of central Bolivia and are Turonian-Santonian in age.

facts.statement: The genus Yacarerani was formally described in 2009 in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
facts.quote: The genus was described in 2009 in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

facts.statement: Fossil material representing two individuals was found in association with eggs believed to be part of a nest.
facts.quote: The material represents two individuals and was found in association with eggs that are thought to have been part of a nest.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Yacarerani may have lived in small groups and created burrows to lay eggs.
facts.quote: It may have lived in small groups, creating burrows to lay eggs in.

facts.statement: Yacarerani possessed heterodont dentition, featuring different tooth shapes in different parts of the jaws.
facts.quote: The dentition of Yacarerani, like many other notosuchians, is heterodont, with different tooth morphologies in different parts of the jaws.

facts.statement: Two teeth in the lower jaw projected forward from the tip, resembling rabbit incisors.
facts.quote: Two teeth in the lower jaw project forward from the tip, resembling the incisors of a rabbit.

facts.statement: Yacarerani is classified within the suborder Notosuchia.
The time range for Yacarerani is recorded as Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Navarro et al. interprets the bone histology of Yacarerani boliviensis as consistent with fast growth dynamics interrupted by periods of decline.
facts.quote: Navarro et al. (2026) study the bone histology of Yacarerani boliviensis, and interpret it as consistent with fast growth dynamics with periods of decline.

rejected.statement: Posterior teeth were cusped and adapted for grinding or chopping food like tubers or small arthropods.
rejected.quote: Other teeth, situated posteriorly, are cusped and adapted for grinding or chopping food such as tubers or small arthropods.

rejected.statement: Yacarerani belongs to the family Sphagesauridae.
